name: env-manager
description: Tracks local .env files: masked tree pane, gitignore checks, add/copy/edit values, and secrets typed into prompts moved into an env file

patterns.title: Env file patterns
patterns.description: Glob patterns of file names to track, separated by spaces or commas. * matches any characters except /.

defaultFile.title: Default env file
defaultFile.description: Where a secret typed into a prompt is stored, relative to the working directory.

intercept.title: Intercept secrets in prompts
intercept.description: on: secrets found in a prompt are moved into the default env file before the model sees them.

guardWrites.title: Guard Claude's writes
guardWrites.description: on: when Claude writes a key into a source file with Write or Edit, the write is refused, the key moves into the default env file and Claude is told to read it from the environment.

scanFiles.title: Scan source files
scanFiles.description: on: the project's files (git-tracked and untracked, not ignored) are scanned for hardcoded keys with gitleaks' rules; findings show in the /env pane.

gitleaks.title: gitleaks history scan
gitleaks.description: Scan the commit history with the gitleaks binary when it is installed. manual: only from the /env settings page. auto: at session start when HEAD moved since the last run. Each run's result is kept per repository.

maxDepth.title: Scan depth
maxDepth.description: How many folder levels below the working directory are scanned.

checkMinutes.title: Leak check interval (minutes)
checkMinutes.description: Minimum minutes between background leak checks at the end of a turn.

renamePrompt.title: Key name prompt
renamePrompt.description: What Claude is told to do after a secret from a prompt is stored: how to report it and how to ask for a key name. Placeholders: {file} the env file, {path} its full path, {stored} the stored key names, {keys} the names already in the file, {tool} the rename tool. Empty: the default. The safety rules (never ask for or print the value) are always added and cannot be edited here.
renamePrompt.default: In your reply, in the user's language: 1) tell them which file path and key name each value was stored under, showing only the masked value. 2) Suggest 3-5 key names that fit the context as a numbered list, best first: consider what the user is doing in this prompt and conversation, the provider the value looks like, the names already in {file} ({keys}), and env variable names the project's code reads (process.env.X, os.environ, getenv). Make the current name {stored} the last option. 3) Ask which one to use. When they pick a number or type a name, call {tool} with { file: "{file}", from: <current key>, to: <new key> }; if they keep the current name, do nothing.
